payload.purpose: answer_incident_question
payload.question: Is this a possible leak or an instrumentation issue? Which pipeline section should an integrity engineer inspect first, and which sensors are unreliable?

cards.title: Distinguish unreliable observations from physical process evidence

sources.boundary: Marine data-quality and anomaly-attribution principles; not validation of gas-pipeline leak classification.

cards.guidance: An unusual reading is not itself a faulty sensor or a physical leak. Separate completeness, currentness, accuracy and provenance. Missing values and invalid sentinels are observation gaps, not measured pressure drops. Inspect persistence and paired disagreement, and seek an independent reference before attributing a hardware fault. A detector's attribution score identifies a contribution, not a physical root cause. Malfunction and a physical event can coexist.
limitations: This is a research-derived heuristic, not a field-approved sensor diagnosis.
No universal threshold or sensor-failure probability is established.
cards.applies_when: Pressure alerts coexist with missing samples, spikes, drift or inconsistent instrument readings.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived guidance; application requires site instrumentation review.
counterexamples: A gap during a real leak does not establish a healthy pipeline.
A genuine process transient can produce a large anomaly score on functioning instruments.
verification_steps: Compare suspect instruments with independent observers and their actual received coverage.
Check calibration, units, clock and maintenance context; preserve unobserved periods.
State which sensor claims were reviewed and which remain unchecked.

cards.title: Check common causes before counting independent corroboration

sources.boundary: Strong, possible, lower-threshold and noisy detections motivate multiscale inspection; not calibrated gas-pipeline attenuation.
sources.reference: User-provided public defense deck, not redistributed

sources.boundary: Motivates prior knowledge and source-quality review; gateway independence requires site instrumentation verification.

cards.guidance: Inspect groups, not isolated alert flags. For pressure-monitoring investigations, a leak hypothesis should be tested against a sustained connected pattern: disruptive changes near the affected region and weaker, related changes farther along the pipes, including below-threshold observations. Compare synchronized profiles, relative magnitudes, timing, recovery and missingness against independent and contrasting instruments. Attenuation is not necessarily monotonic in real branched gas networks; this is a working hypothesis, not a universal law. Scattered impulses, isolated drift or missing data motivate instrumentation checks but can coexist with a leak. Treat hydraulic connectivity and instrumentation dependency as different relationships. Multiple agreeing instruments sharing a gateway, power supply or calibration path may share an error. Correlation is not independence or a confirmed cause. Shared-failure explanations also need observed evidence; do not declare every sensor on a gateway faulty from metadata alone.
limitations: Confirm A/B gateway assignments against the site instrumentation register.
No validated common-cause reliability model is provided.
cards.applies_when: Several instruments show simultaneous changes, particularly paired taps or instruments sharing infrastructure.
cards.review_basis: Dependency-analysis guidance; confirm the site instrumentation dependencies before applying.
counterexamples: Eight taps on one shared conversion path are not eight independent witnesses.
An operating transient can also produce a coherent pressure pattern; attenuation alone cannot identify a leak.
Independent gateways do not exclude an unrecorded shared power or operating cause.
verification_steps: Compare near, farther and weak/quiet connected observers jointly, not only above-threshold supporters.
Contrast a shared-path instrument with an independent observer; compare profiles, valid-sample overlap and graph distances.
Inspect contradictory or asynchronous changes rather than merging branch-level earliest/latest timings into a common onset.
Open applicable maintenance records and check effective revision and scope.

cards.title: Test operating transients as competing explanations

sources.boundary: Review of pressure methods, operating transients and model assumptions; not a site-specific operating procedure.

cards.guidance: Investigate operating changes rather than equating a pressure anomaly with a leak. Compare the observed sign, timing and affected assets with an approved, incident-time-available record. A proposal is not an executed operation, and a superseded record is not current authority. Read the underlying records referenced by a coverage statement. A plausible explanation for one branch does not automatically explain a different pattern elsewhere. Incomplete logs cannot prove that no operation or leak occurred.
limitations: Temporal association is not a causal intervention.
The cited review includes liquid-pipeline methods; its parameters cannot be transferred directly to subsea gas.
cards.applies_when: Pressure changes could coincide with a valve, compressor, setpoint or calibration activity.
cards.review_basis: Research-grounded guidance; apply the current site operating procedure.
counterexamples: A broad positive operating shift does not by itself explain a separate localized negative region.
A real operating change can coexist with a leak or instrumentation fault.
verification_steps: Search affected and contrasting signal regions, not only the proposed inspection branch.
Open current records and distinguish planned, approved and executed activities.
Compare before/after periods near an observed change; note window censoring and retain missingness.

cards.title: Separate a numerical inspection bracket from physical leak localization

sources.boundary: Explains method-dependent localization assumptions; requires verification of site-specific inspection assumptions.

cards.guidance: Use the numerical tool's actual method and retain its assumptions. The default method brackets affected stations against unaffected neighbours. On extended networks, a broad continuous pressure footprint may leave no unaffected neighbours or an overly wide bracket. The pressure-peak-focus fallback can then identify a priority inspection focus from the final five seconds of fully observed paired readings: a unique contiguous pressure-deficit peak, agreeing pairs, independent comparison paths and weaker immediately neighbouring stations whose contrast exceeds the baseline-noise allowance. Missing comparisons, tied/disconnected peaks, inadequate independence and excessive width still withhold a focus. Those comparison stations need not be unaffected. This is a spatial pressure-focus heuristic, not a calibrated hydraulic inverse problem or a guarantee that a physical leak lies inside the interval. Pressure-wave localization requires justified propagation, timing, flow and pipeline assumptions. Do not infer an exact leak coordinate, leak size or leak probability from anomaly magnitude or a research formula without its inputs. Physical intervention still requires the approved site procedure and operator authorization.
limitations: The source review discusses methods with different fluid and deployment assumptions.
Confirm inspection priorities using independent pressure and flow measurements.
cards.applies_when: An engineer requests a leak location or an inspection recommendation from pressure observations.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived inspection guidance; confirm eligibility and site-specific hydraulic assumptions.
counterexamples: A larger pressure residual is not necessarily the nearest sensor to a leak.
Multiple disjoint pressure regions are not resolved by this single-leak bracket.
verification_steps: Check eligibility, paired coverage, observer independence, actual method and bounding comparisons.
State the priority interval and explain whether its neighbours are unaffected or simply weaker; do not call it a confidence interval or confirmed leak point.
Keep physical confirmation and operator authorization separate from the completed pressure-pattern assessment; do not clear alarms while waiting for an LLM.

cards.title: Expert-guided differential investigation program

sources.boundary: Architecture, expertise capture and open uncertainty/contradiction challenges; no subsea benchmark.

cards.guidance: Use this natural-language program to guide the existing read-only specialist workflow, not to assert an answer. Preserve competing leak, instrumentation and operating explanations. Select measurements and contextual checks that could distinguish them, including counterevidence. Apply only relevant knowledge, explicitly connect it to observed case evidence, and retain contradictions and missing prerequisites. Domain guidance supplies reasoning, not incident facts or authority to clear the numerical warning.
limitations: Inspired by DANA CAPTURE/APPLY and natural-language programs, not an OpenSSA or DanaOS implementation.
The paper's FinanceBench results do not establish pipeline diagnostic accuracy.
cards.applies_when: An anomaly episode requires a bounded, reviewable leak-versus-instrumentation RCA investigation.
cards.review_basis: DANA-inspired investigation program; apply site-reviewed expertise and operator approval.
counterexamples: Retrieving a relevant document without applying it is not RCA.
A well-cited but consistently wrong explanation is not successful expert reasoning.
verification_steps: Quality: establish what was measured reliably and what remains missing.
Diagnosis: inspect connectivity, independent domains and competing signal regions.
Diagnosis: choose relevant operational records and discriminating comparisons.
Response: explain which guidance was applied, supporting and contradicting case evidence, and remaining gaps.
Critic: check case facts and knowledge citations against their original pinned sources.
Handoff: request qualified engineer verification; unresolved evidence remains unresolved.

Inspect persistence and paired disagreement, and seek an independent reference before attributing a hardware fault. A detector's attribution score identifies a contribution, not a physical root cause. Malfunction and a physical event can coexist.
limitations: This is a research-derived heuristic, not a field-approved sensor diagnosis.
No universal threshold or sensor-failure probability is established.

cards.title: Separate a numerical inspection bracket from physical leak localization

sources.boundary: Explains method-dependent localization assumptions; requires verification of site-specific inspection assumptions.

cards.guidance: Use the numerical tool's actual method and retain its assumptions. The default method brackets affected stations against unaffected neighbours. On extended networks, a broad continuous pressure footprint may leave no unaffected neighbours or an overly wide bracket. The pressure-peak-focus fallback can then identify a priority inspection focus from the final five seconds of fully observed paired readings: a unique contiguous pressure-deficit peak, agreeing pairs, independent comparison paths and weaker immediately neighbouring stations whose contrast exceeds the baseline-noise allowance. Missing comparisons, tied/disconnected peaks, inadequate independence and excessive width still withhold a focus. Those comparison stations need not be unaffected. This is a spatial pressure-focus heuristic, not a calibrated hydraulic inverse problem or a guarantee that a physical leak lies inside the interval. Pressure-wave localization requires justified propagation, timing, flow and pipeline assumptions. Do not infer an exact leak coordinate, leak size or leak probability from anomaly magnitude or a research formula without its inputs. Physical intervention still requires the approved site procedure and operator authorization.
limitations: The source review discusses methods with different fluid and deployment assumptions.
Confirm inspection priorities using independent pressure and flow measurements.
cards.applies_when: An engineer requests a leak location or an inspection recommendation from pressure observations.

payload.purpose: assess_event_and_location
payload.question: Is this a possible leak or an instrumentation issue? Which pipeline section should an integrity engineer inspect first, and which sensors are unreliable?

cards.title: Distinguish unreliable observations from physical process evidence

sources.boundary: Marine data-quality and anomaly-attribution principles; not validation of gas-pipeline leak classification.

cards.guidance: An unusual reading is not itself a faulty sensor or a physical leak. Separate completeness, currentness, accuracy and provenance. Missing values and invalid sentinels are observation gaps, not measured pressure drops. Inspect persistence and paired disagreement, and seek an independent reference before attributing a hardware fault. A detector's attribution score identifies a contribution, not a physical root cause. Malfunction and a physical event can coexist.
limitations: This is a research-derived heuristic, not a field-approved sensor diagnosis.
No universal threshold or sensor-failure probability is established.
cards.applies_when: Pressure alerts coexist with missing samples, spikes, drift or inconsistent instrument readings.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived guidance; application requires site instrumentation review.
counterexamples: A gap during a real leak does not establish a healthy pipeline.
A genuine process transient can produce a large anomaly score on functioning instruments.
verification_steps: Compare suspect instruments with independent observers and their actual received coverage.
Check calibration, units, clock and maintenance context; preserve unobserved periods.
State which sensor claims were reviewed and which remain unchecked.

cards.title: Check common causes before counting independent corroboration

sources.boundary: Strong, possible, lower-threshold and noisy detections motivate multiscale inspection; not calibrated gas-pipeline attenuation.
sources.reference: User-provided public defense deck, not redistributed

sources.boundary: Motivates prior knowledge and source-quality review; gateway independence requires site instrumentation verification.

cards.guidance: Inspect groups, not isolated alert flags. For pressure-monitoring investigations, a leak hypothesis should be tested against a sustained connected pattern: disruptive changes near the affected region and weaker, related changes farther along the pipes, including below-threshold observations. Compare synchronized profiles, relative magnitudes, timing, recovery and missingness against independent and contrasting instruments. Attenuation is not necessarily monotonic in real branched gas networks; this is a working hypothesis, not a universal law. Scattered impulses, isolated drift or missing data motivate instrumentation checks but can coexist with a leak. Treat hydraulic connectivity and instrumentation dependency as different relationships. Multiple agreeing instruments sharing a gateway, power supply or calibration path may share an error. Correlation is not independence or a confirmed cause. Shared-failure explanations also need observed evidence; do not declare every sensor on a gateway faulty from metadata alone.
limitations: Confirm A/B gateway assignments against the site instrumentation register.
No validated common-cause reliability model is provided.
cards.applies_when: Several instruments show simultaneous changes, particularly paired taps or instruments sharing infrastructure.
cards.review_basis: Dependency-analysis guidance; confirm the site instrumentation dependencies before applying.
counterexamples: Eight taps on one shared conversion path are not eight independent witnesses.
An operating transient can also produce a coherent pressure pattern; attenuation alone cannot identify a leak.
Independent gateways do not exclude an unrecorded shared power or operating cause.
verification_steps: Compare near, farther and weak/quiet connected observers jointly, not only above-threshold supporters.
Contrast a shared-path instrument with an independent observer; compare profiles, valid-sample overlap and graph distances.
Inspect contradictory or asynchronous changes rather than merging branch-level earliest/latest timings into a common onset.
Open applicable maintenance records and check effective revision and scope.

cards.title: Test operating transients as competing explanations

sources.boundary: Review of pressure methods, operating transients and model assumptions; not a site-specific operating procedure.

cards.guidance: Investigate operating changes rather than equating a pressure anomaly with a leak. Compare the observed sign, timing and affected assets with an approved, incident-time-available record. A proposal is not an executed operation, and a superseded record is not current authority. Read the underlying records referenced by a coverage statement. A plausible explanation for one branch does not automatically explain a different pattern elsewhere. Incomplete logs cannot prove that no operation or leak occurred.
limitations: Temporal association is not a causal intervention.
The cited review includes liquid-pipeline methods; its parameters cannot be transferred directly to subsea gas.
cards.applies_when: Pressure changes could coincide with a valve, compressor, setpoint or calibration activity.
cards.review_basis: Research-grounded guidance; apply the current site operating procedure.
counterexamples: A broad positive operating shift does not by itself explain a separate localized negative region.
A real operating change can coexist with a leak or instrumentation fault.
verification_steps: Search affected and contrasting signal regions, not only the proposed inspection branch.
Open current records and distinguish planned, approved and executed activities.
Compare before/after periods near an observed change; note window censoring and retain missingness.

cards.title: Separate a numerical inspection bracket from physical leak localization

sources.boundary: Explains method-dependent localization assumptions; requires verification of site-specific inspection assumptions.

cards.guidance: Use the numerical tool's actual method and retain its assumptions. The default method brackets affected stations against unaffected neighbours. On extended networks, a broad continuous pressure footprint may leave no unaffected neighbours or an overly wide bracket. The pressure-peak-focus fallback can then identify a priority inspection focus from the final five seconds of fully observed paired readings: a unique contiguous pressure-deficit peak, agreeing pairs, independent comparison paths and weaker immediately neighbouring stations whose contrast exceeds the baseline-noise allowance. Missing comparisons, tied/disconnected peaks, inadequate independence and excessive width still withhold a focus. Those comparison stations need not be unaffected. This is a spatial pressure-focus heuristic, not a calibrated hydraulic inverse problem or a guarantee that a physical leak lies inside the interval. Pressure-wave localization requires justified propagation, timing, flow and pipeline assumptions. Do not infer an exact leak coordinate, leak size or leak probability from anomaly magnitude or a research formula without its inputs. Physical intervention still requires the approved site procedure and operator authorization.
limitations: The source review discusses methods with different fluid and deployment assumptions.
Confirm inspection priorities using independent pressure and flow measurements.
cards.applies_when: An engineer requests a leak location or an inspection recommendation from pressure observations.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived inspection guidance; confirm eligibility and site-specific hydraulic assumptions.
counterexamples: A larger pressure residual is not necessarily the nearest sensor to a leak.
Multiple disjoint pressure regions are not resolved by this single-leak bracket.
verification_steps: Check eligibility, paired coverage, observer independence, actual method and bounding comparisons.
State the priority interval and explain whether its neighbours are unaffected or simply weaker; do not call it a confidence interval or confirmed leak point.
Keep physical confirmation and operator authorization separate from the completed pressure-pattern assessment; do not clear alarms while waiting for an LLM.

cards.title: Expert-guided differential investigation program

sources.boundary: Architecture, expertise capture and open uncertainty/contradiction challenges; no subsea benchmark.

cards.guidance: Use this natural-language program to guide the existing read-only specialist workflow, not to assert an answer. Preserve competing leak, instrumentation and operating explanations. Select measurements and contextual checks that could distinguish them, including counterevidence. Apply only relevant knowledge, explicitly connect it to observed case evidence, and retain contradictions and missing prerequisites. Domain guidance supplies reasoning, not incident facts or authority to clear the numerical warning.
limitations: Inspired by DANA CAPTURE/APPLY and natural-language programs, not an OpenSSA or DanaOS implementation.
The paper's FinanceBench results do not establish pipeline diagnostic accuracy.

payload.question: Is this a possible leak or an instrumentation issue? Which pipeline section should an integrity engineer inspect first, and which sensors are unreliable?

cards.title: Distinguish unreliable observations from physical process evidence

sources.boundary: Marine data-quality and anomaly-attribution principles; not validation of gas-pipeline leak classification.

cards.guidance: An unusual reading is not itself a faulty sensor or a physical leak. Separate completeness, currentness, accuracy and provenance. Missing values and invalid sentinels are observation gaps, not measured pressure drops. Inspect persistence and paired disagreement, and seek an independent reference before attributing a hardware fault. A detector's attribution score identifies a contribution, not a physical root cause. Malfunction and a physical event can coexist.
limitations: This is a research-derived heuristic, not a field-approved sensor diagnosis.
No universal threshold or sensor-failure probability is established.
cards.applies_when: Pressure alerts coexist with missing samples, spikes, drift or inconsistent instrument readings.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived guidance; application requires site instrumentation review.
counterexamples: A gap during a real leak does not establish a healthy pipeline.
A genuine process transient can produce a large anomaly score on functioning instruments.
verification_steps: Compare suspect instruments with independent observers and their actual received coverage.
Check calibration, units, clock and maintenance context; preserve unobserved periods.
State which sensor claims were reviewed and which remain unchecked.

cards.title: Check common causes before counting independent corroboration

sources.boundary: Strong, possible, lower-threshold and noisy detections motivate multiscale inspection; not calibrated gas-pipeline attenuation.
sources.reference: User-provided public defense deck, not redistributed

sources.boundary: Motivates prior knowledge and source-quality review; gateway independence requires site instrumentation verification.

cards.guidance: Inspect groups, not isolated alert flags. For pressure-monitoring investigations, a leak hypothesis should be tested against a sustained connected pattern: disruptive changes near the affected region and weaker, related changes farther along the pipes, including below-threshold observations. Compare synchronized profiles, relative magnitudes, timing, recovery and missingness against independent and contrasting instruments. Attenuation is not necessarily monotonic in real branched gas networks; this is a working hypothesis, not a universal law. Scattered impulses, isolated drift or missing data motivate instrumentation checks but can coexist with a leak. Treat hydraulic connectivity and instrumentation dependency as different relationships. Multiple agreeing instruments sharing a gateway, power supply or calibration path may share an error. Correlation is not independence or a confirmed cause. Shared-failure explanations also need observed evidence; do not declare every sensor on a gateway faulty from metadata alone.
limitations: Confirm A/B gateway assignments against the site instrumentation register.
No validated common-cause reliability model is provided.
cards.applies_when: Several instruments show simultaneous changes, particularly paired taps or instruments sharing infrastructure.
cards.review_basis: Dependency-analysis guidance; confirm the site instrumentation dependencies before applying.
counterexamples: Eight taps on one shared conversion path are not eight independent witnesses.
An operating transient can also produce a coherent pressure pattern; attenuation alone cannot identify a leak.
Independent gateways do not exclude an unrecorded shared power or operating cause.
verification_steps: Compare near, farther and weak/quiet connected observers jointly, not only above-threshold supporters.
Contrast a shared-path instrument with an independent observer; compare profiles, valid-sample overlap and graph distances.
Inspect contradictory or asynchronous changes rather than merging branch-level earliest/latest timings into a common onset.
Open applicable maintenance records and check effective revision and scope.

cards.title: Test operating transients as competing explanations

sources.boundary: Review of pressure methods, operating transients and model assumptions; not a site-specific operating procedure.

cards.guidance: Investigate operating changes rather than equating a pressure anomaly with a leak. Compare the observed sign, timing and affected assets with an approved, incident-time-available record. A proposal is not an executed operation, and a superseded record is not current authority. Read the underlying records referenced by a coverage statement. A plausible explanation for one branch does not automatically explain a different pattern elsewhere. Incomplete logs cannot prove that no operation or leak occurred.
limitations: Temporal association is not a causal intervention.
The cited review includes liquid-pipeline methods; its parameters cannot be transferred directly to subsea gas.
cards.applies_when: Pressure changes could coincide with a valve, compressor, setpoint or calibration activity.
cards.review_basis: Research-grounded guidance; apply the current site operating procedure.
counterexamples: A broad positive operating shift does not by itself explain a separate localized negative region.
A real operating change can coexist with a leak or instrumentation fault.
verification_steps: Search affected and contrasting signal regions, not only the proposed inspection branch.
Open current records and distinguish planned, approved and executed activities.
Compare before/after periods near an observed change; note window censoring and retain missingness.

cards.title: Separate a numerical inspection bracket from physical leak localization

sources.boundary: Explains method-dependent localization assumptions; requires verification of site-specific inspection assumptions.

cards.guidance: Use the numerical tool's actual method and retain its assumptions. The default method brackets affected stations against unaffected neighbours. On extended networks, a broad continuous pressure footprint may leave no unaffected neighbours or an overly wide bracket. The pressure-peak-focus fallback can then identify a priority inspection focus from the final five seconds of fully observed paired readings: a unique contiguous pressure-deficit peak, agreeing pairs, independent comparison paths and weaker immediately neighbouring stations whose contrast exceeds the baseline-noise allowance. Missing comparisons, tied/disconnected peaks, inadequate independence and excessive width still withhold a focus. Those comparison stations need not be unaffected. This is a spatial pressure-focus heuristic, not a calibrated hydraulic inverse problem or a guarantee that a physical leak lies inside the interval. Pressure-wave localization requires justified propagation, timing, flow and pipeline assumptions. Do not infer an exact leak coordinate, leak size or leak probability from anomaly magnitude or a research formula without its inputs. Physical intervention still requires the approved site procedure and operator authorization.
limitations: The source review discusses methods with different fluid and deployment assumptions.
Confirm inspection priorities using independent pressure and flow measurements.
cards.applies_when: An engineer requests a leak location or an inspection recommendation from pressure observations.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived inspection guidance; confirm eligibility and site-specific hydraulic assumptions.
counterexamples: A larger pressure residual is not necessarily the nearest sensor to a leak.
Multiple disjoint pressure regions are not resolved by this single-leak bracket.
verification_steps: Check eligibility, paired coverage, observer independence, actual method and bounding comparisons.
State the priority interval and explain whether its neighbours are unaffected or simply weaker; do not call it a confidence interval or confirmed leak point.
Keep physical confirmation and operator authorization separate from the completed pressure-pattern assessment; do not clear alarms while waiting for an LLM.

cards.title: Expert-guided differential investigation program

sources.boundary: Architecture, expertise capture and open uncertainty/contradiction challenges; no subsea benchmark.

cards.guidance: Use this natural-language program to guide the existing read-only specialist workflow, not to assert an answer. Preserve competing leak, instrumentation and operating explanations. Select measurements and contextual checks that could distinguish them, including counterevidence. Apply only relevant knowledge, explicitly connect it to observed case evidence, and retain contradictions and missing prerequisites. Domain guidance supplies reasoning, not incident facts or authority to clear the numerical warning.
limitations: Inspired by DANA CAPTURE/APPLY and natural-language programs, not an OpenSSA or DanaOS implementation.
The paper's FinanceBench results do not establish pipeline diagnostic accuracy.
cards.applies_when: An anomaly episode requires a bounded, reviewable leak-versus-instrumentation RCA investigation.
cards.review_basis: DANA-inspired investigation program; apply site-reviewed expertise and operator approval.
counterexamples: Retrieving a relevant document without applying it is not RCA.
A well-cited but consistently wrong explanation is not successful expert reasoning.
verification_steps: Quality: establish what was measured reliably and what remains missing.
Diagnosis: inspect connectivity, independent domains and competing signal regions.
Diagnosis: choose relevant operational records and discriminating comparisons.
Response: explain which guidance was applied, supporting and contradicting case evidence, and remaining gaps.
Critic: check case facts and knowledge citations against their original pinned sources.
Handoff: request qualified engineer verification; unresolved evidence remains unresolved.

Decision
Prioritize integrity review on P5, using the accepted 600-1000 m inspection interval measured along the pipe, around stations ST4 and ST5. P5 has the strongest supported joint pressure-loss pattern and is the suspected integrity incident. This numerical pressure-focus interval is an inspection priority, not a confirmed leak point or dispatch approval [claim-114; KN-LOCALIZATION-R1]. Keep P7 on the shared-connection instrumentation track, P2 on operating-transition/process review, and P4 on secondary pressure/process review rather than diagnosing a second leak.

Your first actions
1. Scope the P5 integrity desk review to 600-1000 m, retaining ST3 and ST6 as weaker bounding comparisons; use the accepted focus without guessing a physical leak coordinate [claim-114; KN-LOCALIZATION-R1].
2. Keep gateway-P7-0, the shared data connection for both sensors at P7 stations ST1, ST3, ST5 and ST7, on instrumentation review; distinguish these suspect readings from the stable ST2 comparison [MAINT-P7-GW-002; 23f576aa-0515-5370-a23c-174c0fab18c1].
3. Use the already-reviewed P2 pressure-setting record to distinguish its earlier rise from the final pressure loss; keep P4 ST1/ST2 as secondary pressure observations, not faulty-sensor findings [OP-P2-EXTENDED-001; 0b9dba44-d3fc-5573-9af5-88562544103d].
4. Request independent physical pressure/flow confirmation for the P5 focus and a pressure reference outside gateway-P7-0; these distinguish physical loss from shared measurement bias without delaying the supported review priorities [KN-INDEPENDENCE-R1; KN-LOCALIZATION-R1].

Already checked
Specialists compared paired sensors, meaning two sensors at each station, through elapsed seconds 0-150 of the recording. P5 developed sustained losses around seconds 91-97, with agreement across two shared data connections. In the final five seconds, elapsed seconds 145-150, P5-ST4-A was 1.667 bar below the supplied normal reference, versus 1.247 bar at neighboring P5-ST3-A; bar is a pressure unit [ev-142; ev-138]. P4-ST1-A was only 0.188 bar below reference [ev-098]. P2's earlier positive change broadly matches the logged approximately 0.4-bar rise during seconds 90-145, but its final-five-second readings are below reference: 0.024 bar at ST1-A and 0.167 bar at ST8-A [ev-034; ev-062]. The record's end does not establish recovery.

Why this decision
P7-ST1-A remains 0.722 bar below reference in those final five seconds [ev-194]. Its observed persistent offset, a reading shifted to another level, affects P7-ST1-A/B, P7-ST3-A/B, P7-ST5-A/B and P7-ST7-A/B and matches the revised calibration context. These readings are suspect; individual hardware faults are not established. P2/P4 screening spike flags do not establish unreliable instruments when profiles show joint pressure changes [KN-QUALITY-R1]. All 6720 expected samples were usable, with no measured missing/invalid coverage loss; the health review remains partial, so completeness does not certify every sensor's accuracy [ev-225].

What changes the decision
An independent sustained P7 loss outside its shared connection, continued P2 loss beyond the recorded transition, or worsening P5 pressure would change the respective attention tracks. P4's weaker changes may accompany the primary incident, but their relationship remains unresolved. Incomplete operating logs leave competing P5 causes open; pressure agreement establishes a review priority, not a confirmed physical cause [LOG-EXTENDED-COVERAGE-001; KN-INDEPENDENCE-R1; KN-OPERATING-R1].

sources.boundary: Marine data-quality and anomaly-attribution principles; not validation of gas-pipeline leak classification.

cards.guidance: An unusual reading is not itself a faulty sensor or a physical leak. Separate completeness, currentness, accuracy and provenance. Missing values and invalid sentinels are observation gaps, not measured pressure drops. Inspect persistence and paired disagreement, and seek an independent reference before attributing a hardware fault. cards.guidance: Inspect groups, not isolated alert flags. For pressure-monitoring investigations, a leak hypothesis should be tested against a sustained connected pattern: disruptive changes near the affected region and weaker, related changes farther along the pipes, including below-threshold observations. Compare synchronized profiles, relative magnitudes, timing, recovery and missingness against independent and contrasting instruments. Attenuation is not necessarily monotonic in real branched gas networks; this is a working hypothesis, not a universal law. Scattered impulses, isolated drift or missing data motivate instrumentation checks but can coexist with a leak. Treat hydraulic connectivity and instrumentation dependency as different relationships. Multiple agreeing instruments sharing a gateway, power supply or calibration path may share an error. Correlation is not independence or a confirmed cause. Shared-failure explanations also need observed evidence; do not declare every sensor on a gateway faulty from metadata alone.

cards.title: Separate a numerical inspection bracket from physical leak localization

sources.boundary: Explains method-dependent localization assumptions; requires verification of site-specific inspection assumptions.

cards.guidance: Use the numerical tool's actual method and retain its assumptions. The default method brackets affected stations against unaffected neighbours. On extended networks, a broad continuous pressure footprint may leave no unaffected neighbours or an overly wide bracket. The pressure-peak-focus fallback can then identify a priority inspection focus from the final five seconds of fully observed paired readings: a unique contiguous pressure-deficit peak, agreeing pairs, independent comparison paths and weaker immediately neighbouring stations whose contrast exceeds the baseline-noise allowance. Missing comparisons, tied/disconnected peaks, inadequate independence and excessive width still withhold a focus. Those comparison stations need not be unaffected. This is a spatial pressure-focus heuristic, not a calibrated hydraulic inverse problem or a guarantee that a physical leak lies inside the interval. Pressure-wave localization requires justified propagation, timing, flow and pipeline assumptions. Do not infer an exact leak coordinate, leak size or leak probability from anomaly magnitude or a research formula without its inputs. Physical intervention still requires the approved site procedure and operator authorization.
limitations: The source review discusses methods with different fluid and deployment assumptions.

ENGINEER QUESTION
Is this a possible leak or an instrumentation issue? Which pipeline section should an integrity engineer inspect first, and which sensors are unreliable?
ENGINEERING ASSESSMENT
Decision
Prioritize integrity review on P5 at the accepted 600-1000 m inspection interval, measured along the pipe around stations ST4/ST5. Its joint pressure-loss pattern supports a suspected integrity incident. This spatial pressure-focus heuristic identifies an inspection priority, not a confirmed leak point or dispatch approval [claim-114; KN-LOCALIZATION-R1]. Keep P7 on shared-connection instrumentation review, P2 on operating-transition/process review, and P4 on secondary pressure/process review, not a second leak diagnosis.

Your first actions
1. Scope P5 integrity desk review to 600-1000 m, retaining ST3/ST6 as weaker bounding comparisons rather than guessing a leak coordinate [claim-114; KN-LOCALIZATION-R1].
2. Keep gateway-P7-0, the shared data connection serving both sensors at P7 ST1/ST3/ST5/ST7, on instrumentation review; distinguish its suspect readings from the stable ST2 comparison [MAINT-P7-GW-002; 23f576aa-0515-5370-a23c-174c0fab18c1].
3. Use the already-reviewed P2 pressure-setting record to separate its earlier rise from its ending loss; retain P4 ST1/ST2 as secondary pressure observations, not faulty-sensor findings [OP-P2-EXTENDED-001; 0b9dba44-d3fc-5573-9af5-88562544103d].
4. Request independent physical pressure/flow confirmation for P5 and a pressure reference outside gateway-P7-0 to distinguish physical loss from shared measurement bias [KN-INDEPENDENCE-R1; KN-LOCALIZATION-R1].

Already checked
Specialists compared paired sensors—two sensors at each station—through elapsed seconds 0-150 of the recording. P5-ST4-A's sustained deficit begins at second 91 and P5-ST3-A's at second 92 [ev-142; ev-138]; comparisons show agreement across two data connections. In the final five seconds, elapsed seconds 145-150, ST4-A is 1.667 bar below the supplied normal reference versus 1.247 bar at neighboring ST3-A; bar is a pressure unit. P4-ST1-A is only 0.188 bar below reference [ev-098]. P2's earlier rise broadly matches the logged approximately 0.4-bar rise during seconds 90-145, but final-five-second deficits are 0.024 bar at ST1-A and 0.167 bar at ST8-A [ev-034; ev-062]. The record's end does not establish recovery.

Why this decision
P7-ST1-A remains 0.722 bar below reference in those final five seconds [ev-194]. Persistent offsets—readings shifted to another level—affect P7-ST1-A/B, P7-ST3-A/B, P7-ST5-A/B and P7-ST7-A/B, matching the revised calibration context. These readings are suspect, not confirmed hardware failures. P2/P4 screening spike flags do not establish unreliable instruments when profiles show joint pressure changes [KN-QUALITY-R1]. All 6720 expected samples were usable; no missing/invalid coverage loss was measured. Health review remains partial, so completeness does not certify every sensor's accuracy [ev-225].

What changes the decision
An independent sustained P7 loss outside its shared connection, continued P2 loss beyond the recorded transition, or worsening P5 pressure would change their attention tracks. P4's weaker changes may accompany the primary incident, but their relationship remains unresolved. Incomplete operating logs leave competing P5 causes open; pressure agreement establishes review priority, not physical cause [LOG-EXTENDED-COVERAGE-001; KN-INDEPENDENCE-R1; KN-OPERATING-R1].

Historical profiles show a developing loss rather than a stationary baseline offset, and the final-five-second deficit at P5-ST4-A is 1.667 bar below the supplied reference during elapsed seconds 145-150. The accepted P5 600-1000 m focus is a spatial pressure heuristic, not hydraulic localization or proof that a leak lies inside it. P4's weaker paired losses are secondary observations whose relationship to P5 is unresolved, not evidence for a separately prioritized leak. Independent pressure/flow confirmation and more complete operating context would distinguish physical loss from the remaining competing explanations.

ENGINEER QUESTION
Is this a possible leak or an instrumentation issue? Which pipeline section should an integrity engineer inspect first, and which sensors are unreliable?
ENGINEERING ASSESSMENT
Decision
Prioritize integrity review on P5 at the accepted 600-1000 m inspection interval, measured along the pipe around stations ST4/ST5. Its joint pressure-loss pattern supports a suspected integrity incident. This spatial pressure-focus heuristic identifies an inspection priority, not a confirmed leak point or dispatch approval [claim-114; KN-LOCALIZATION-R1]. Keep P7 on shared-connection instrumentation review, P2 on operating-transition/process review, and P4 on secondary pressure/process review, not a second leak diagnosis.

Your first actions
1. Scope P5 integrity desk review to 600-1000 m, retaining ST3/ST6 as weaker bounding comparisons rather than guessing a leak coordinate [claim-114; KN-LOCALIZATION-R1].
2. Keep gateway-P7-0, the shared data connection serving both sensors at P7 ST1/ST3/ST5/ST7, on instrumentation review; distinguish its suspect readings from the stable ST2 comparison [MAINT-P7-GW-002; 23f576aa-0515-5370-a23c-174c0fab18c1].
3. Use the already-reviewed P2 pressure-setting record to separate its earlier rise from its ending loss; retain P4 ST1/ST2 as secondary pressure observations, not faulty-sensor findings [OP-P2-EXTENDED-001; 0b9dba44-d3fc-5573-9af5-88562544103d].
4. Request independent physical pressure/flow confirmation for P5 and a pressure reference outside gateway-P7-0 to distinguish physical loss from shared measurement bias [KN-INDEPENDENCE-R1; KN-LOCALIZATION-R1].

Already checked
Specialists compared paired sensors—two sensors at each station—through elapsed seconds 0-150 of the recording. P5-ST4-A's sustained deficit begins at second 91 and P5-ST3-A's at second 92 [ev-142; ev-138]; comparisons show agreement across two data connections. In the final five seconds, elapsed seconds 145-150, ST4-A is 1.667 bar below the supplied normal reference versus 1.247 bar at neighboring ST3-A; bar is a pressure unit. P4-ST1-A is only 0.188 bar below reference [ev-098]. P2's earlier rise broadly matches the logged approximately 0.4-bar rise during seconds 90-145, but final-five-second deficits are 0.024 bar at ST1-A and 0.167 bar at ST8-A [ev-034; ev-062]. The record's end does not establish recovery.

Why this decision
P7-ST1-A remains 0.722 bar below reference in those final five seconds [ev-194]. Persistent offsets—readings shifted to another level—affect P7-ST1-A/B, P7-ST3-A/B, P7-ST5-A/B and P7-ST7-A/B, matching the revised calibration context. These readings are suspect, not confirmed hardware failures. P2/P4 screening spike flags do not establish unreliable instruments when profiles show joint pressure changes [KN-QUALITY-R1]. All 6720 expected samples were usable; no missing/invalid coverage loss was measured. Health review remains partial, so completeness does not certify every sensor's accuracy [ev-225].

What changes the decision
An independent sustained P7 loss outside its shared connection, continued P2 loss beyond the recorded transition, or worsening P5 pressure would change their attention tracks. P4's weaker changes may accompany the primary incident, but their relationship remains unresolved. Incomplete operating logs leave competing P5 causes open; pressure agreement establishes review priority, not physical cause [LOG-EXTENDED-COVERAGE-001; KN-INDEPENDENCE-R1; KN-OPERATING-R1].

COMPETING EXPLANATIONS
leak (possible): P5 supports a possible leak pattern: all eight stations have sustained pressure deficits, with agreeing paired sensors and observations across two gateways. Historical profiles show a developing loss rather than a stationary baseline offset, and the final-five-second deficit at P5-ST4-A is 1.667 bar below the supplied reference during elapsed seconds 145-150. The accepted P5 600-1000 m focus is a spatial pressure heuristic, not hydraulic localization or proof that a leak lies inside it. P4's weaker paired losses are secondary observations whose relationship to P5 is unresolved, not evidence for a separately prioritized leak. Independent pressure/flow confirmation and more complete operating context would distinguish physical loss from the remaining competing explanations.

Their historical before/after changes are about -0.725 to -0.752 bar over elapsed seconds 0-150 split at second 75, consistent with the revised calibration record's approximately -0.75-bar offset beginning at second 90. These eight taps share gateway-P7-0 and cannot be counted as eight independent witnesses; this supports checking their common measurement connection, not declaring eight hardware failures. The final-five-second deficit at P7-ST1-A is still 0.722 bar during elapsed seconds 145-150, so the problem has not disappeared. answer.text:
Decision
Prioritize integrity review on P5 at the accepted 600-1000 m inspection interval, measured along the pipe around stations ST4/ST5. Its joint pressure-loss pattern supports a suspected integrity incident. This spatial pressure-focus heuristic identifies an inspection priority, not a confirmed leak point or dispatch approval [claim-114; KN-LOCALIZATION-R1]. Keep P7 on shared-connection instrumentation review, P2 on operating-transition/process review, and P4 on secondary pressure/process review, not a second leak diagnosis.

Your first actions
1. Scope P5 integrity desk review to 600-1000 m, retaining ST3/ST6 as weaker bounding comparisons rather than guessing a leak coordinate [claim-114; KN-LOCALIZATION-R1].
2. Keep gateway-P7-0, the shared data connection serving both sensors at P7 ST1/ST3/ST5/ST7, on instrumentation review; distinguish its suspect readings from the stable ST2 comparison [MAINT-P7-GW-002; 23f576aa-0515-5370-a23c-174c0fab18c1].
3. Use the already-reviewed P2 pressure-setting record to separate its earlier rise from its ending loss; retain P4 ST1/ST2 as secondary pressure observations, not faulty-sensor findings [OP-P2-EXTENDED-001; 0b9dba44-d3fc-5573-9af5-88562544103d].
4. Request independent physical pressure/flow confirmation for P5 and a pressure reference outside gateway-P7-0 to distinguish physical loss from shared measurement bias [KN-INDEPENDENCE-R1; KN-LOCALIZATION-R1].

Already checked
Specialists compared paired sensors—two sensors at each station—through elapsed seconds 0-150 of the recording. P5-ST4-A's sustained deficit begins at second 91 and P5-ST3-A's at second 92 [ev-142; ev-138]; comparisons show agreement across two data connections. In the final five seconds, elapsed seconds 145-150, ST4-A is 1.667 bar below the supplied normal reference versus 1.247 bar at neighboring ST3-A; bar is a pressure unit. P4-ST1-A is only 0.188 bar below reference [ev-098]. P2's earlier rise broadly matches the logged approximately 0.4-bar rise during seconds 90-145, but final-five-second deficits are 0.024 bar at ST1-A and 0.167 bar at ST8-A [ev-034; ev-062]. The record's end does not establish recovery.

Why this decision
P7-ST1-A remains 0.722 bar below reference in those final five seconds [ev-194]. Persistent offsets—readings shifted to another level—affect P7-ST1-A/B, P7-ST3-A/B, P7-ST5-A/B and P7-ST7-A/B, matching the revised calibration context. These readings are suspect, not confirmed hardware failures. P2/P4 screening spike flags do not establish unreliable instruments when profiles show joint pressure changes [KN-QUALITY-R1]. All 6720 expected samples were usable; no missing/invalid coverage loss was measured. Health review remains partial, so completeness does not certify every sensor's accuracy [ev-225].

What changes the decision
An independent sustained P7 loss outside its shared connection, continued P2 loss beyond the recorded transition, or worsening P5 pressure would change their attention tracks. P4's weaker changes may accompany the primary incident, but their relationship remains unresolved. Incomplete operating logs leave competing P5 causes open; pressure agreement establishes review priority, not physical cause [LOG-EXTENDED-COVERAGE-001; KN-INDEPENDENCE-R1; KN-OPERATING-R1].

competing_causes.text: P5 supports a possible leak pattern: all eight stations have sustained pressure deficits, with agreeing paired sensors and observations across two gateways. Historical profiles show a developing loss rather than a stationary baseline offset, and the final-five-second deficit at P5-ST4-A is 1.667 bar below the supplied reference during elapsed seconds 145-150. The accepted P5 600-1000 m focus is a spatial pressure heuristic, not hydraulic localization or proof that a leak lies inside it. P4's weaker paired losses are secondary observations whose relationship to P5 is unresolved, not evidence for a separately prioritized leak. Independent pressure/flow confirmation and more complete operating context would distinguish physical loss from the remaining competing explanations.

P7 has concrete shared-path evidence: both taps at ST1, ST3, ST5 and ST7 shift persistently downward, while the executed ST2 comparison stays approximately unchanged. Their historical before/after changes are about -0.725 to -0.752 bar over elapsed seconds 0-150 split at second 75, consistent with the revised calibration record's approximately -0.75-bar offset beginning at second 90. These eight taps share gateway-P7-0 and cannot be counted as eight independent witnesses; this supports checking their common measurement connection, not declaring eight hardware failures. The final-five-second deficit at P7-ST1-A is still 0.722 bar during elapsed seconds 145-150, so the problem has not disappeared. A pressure reference outside that connection is needed to distinguish the suspected measurement bias from concurrent physical pressure loss.

P2's historical profiles show a broad paired rise around the recorded pressure-setting transition, with before/after increases of 0.182-0.344 bar across the comparison spanning elapsed seconds 0-150 and split at second 75. Its positive sign, broad footprint and timing are consistent with the opened record's approximately 0.4-bar expected rise during seconds 90-145, although the measured magnitude varies along the branch. In the final five seconds, seconds 145-150, ST1-A and ST8-A instead read 0.024 and 0.167 bar below the supplied reference; the earlier rise must not substitute for current pressure. There is no supported joint leak pattern in this window on P2, but the ending loss deserves process attention beyond the recorded period. This record does not explain P5's separate negative focus, and incomplete logs do not exclude additional operations or a coincident event.

regional_assessments.text: P5's priority pair groups at ST4/ST5, 700/900 m along the pipe, are 1.651-1.673 bar below the supplied reference in the final five seconds, elapsed seconds 145-150; neighboring ST3 is 1.247-1.250 bar below and ST6 is 1.204-1.235 bar below. Their executed historical profiles show sustained losses developing around second 90 and strong within-station agreement across two gateways, supporting integrity review rather than an identified instrument problem. The accepted 600-1000 m interval uses this unique pressure-deficit peak and weaker neighbors, which need not be unaffected; its method is a spatial heuristic, not a confirmed physical leak location. P4 ST1 is only 0.188-0.193 bar below reference and ST2 0.110-0.118 bar below in the same final five seconds, with historical paired losses rather than evidence of isolated faulty spikes. Keep P4 on secondary pressure/process review: its relationship to the P5 incident remains unresolved, while independent pressure/flow confirmation and complete operating context remain necessary for causal attribution.

In the final five seconds, elapsed seconds 145-150, paired P7 deficits below the supplied reference are 0.676-0.722 bar at ST1, 0.707-0.712 at ST3, 0.725-0.741 at ST5 and 0.710-0.726 at ST7. In contrast, the reviewed ST2 pair is 0.036-0.051 bar above reference and its historical profile remains approximately unchanged. The affected eight taps share gateway-P7-0, and their persistent downward offsets match the timing and approximate size described in the revised calibration record; agreement within this common connection is not independent physical corroboration. Prioritize the connection and these exact affected readings for instrumentation review, without labelling ST2 suspect or claiming confirmed hardware faults. An independent pressure reference outside gateway-P7-0 would test the measurement explanation; a sustained independent loss would move P7 toward integrity review rather than assuming calibration excludes a physical event.

The selected P2 station pairs have these final-five-second departures from the supplied reference during elapsed seconds 145-150: ST1 is 0.011-0.024 bar below, ST7 is 0.097-0.120 bar below and ST8 is 0.167-0.186 bar below. ST2 contrasts slightly: ST2-A is 0.009 bar above reference while ST2-B is 0.012 bar below. Separately, the executed historical comparison shows positive before/after shifts across P2, with profiles rising around the logged operating period rather than independent isolated spikes. The record's positive sign, approximately 0.4-bar expected size and seconds 90-145 timing broadly match that earlier rise, but do not explain away the final losses or establish recovery at the record's end. Keep P2 on process review, with no supported joint leak pattern in this window and no demonstrated unreliable ST8 sensor from screening spike counts alone; independent confirmation of whether the ending pressure loss persists beyond the recorded transition would distinguish an operating response from a new event.

payload.question: Is this a possible leak or an instrumentation issue? Which pipeline section should an integrity engineer inspect first, and which sensors are unreliable?

cards.title: Distinguish unreliable observations from physical process evidence

sources.boundary: Marine data-quality and anomaly-attribution principles; not validation of gas-pipeline leak classification.

cards.guidance: An unusual reading is not itself a faulty sensor or a physical leak. Separate completeness, currentness, accuracy and provenance. Missing values and invalid sentinels are observation gaps, not measured pressure drops. Inspect persistence and paired disagreement, and seek an independent reference before attributing a hardware fault. A detector's attribution score identifies a contribution, not a physical root cause. Malfunction and a physical event can coexist.
limitations: This is a research-derived heuristic, not a field-approved sensor diagnosis.
No universal threshold or sensor-failure probability is established.
cards.applies_when: Pressure alerts coexist with missing samples, spikes, drift or inconsistent instrument readings.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived guidance; application requires site instrumentation review.
counterexamples: A gap during a real leak does not establish a healthy pipeline.
A genuine process transient can produce a large anomaly score on functioning instruments.
verification_steps: Compare suspect instruments with independent observers and their actual received coverage.
Check calibration, units, clock and maintenance context; preserve unobserved periods.
State which sensor claims were reviewed and which remain unchecked.

cards.title: Check common causes before counting independent corroboration

sources.boundary: Strong, possible, lower-threshold and noisy detections motivate multiscale inspection; not calibrated gas-pipeline attenuation.
sources.reference: User-provided public defense deck, not redistributed

sources.boundary: Motivates prior knowledge and source-quality review; gateway independence requires site instrumentation verification.

cards.guidance: Inspect groups, not isolated alert flags. For pressure-monitoring investigations, a leak hypothesis should be tested against a sustained connected pattern: disruptive changes near the affected region and weaker, related changes farther along the pipes, including below-threshold observations. Compare synchronized profiles, relative magnitudes, timing, recovery and missingness against independent and contrasting instruments. Attenuation is not necessarily monotonic in real branched gas networks; this is a working hypothesis, not a universal law. Scattered impulses, isolated drift or missing data motivate instrumentation checks but can coexist with a leak. Treat hydraulic connectivity and instrumentation dependency as different relationships. Multiple agreeing instruments sharing a gateway, power supply or calibration path may share an error. Correlation is not independence or a confirmed cause. Shared-failure explanations also need observed evidence; do not declare every sensor on a gateway faulty from metadata alone.
limitations: Confirm A/B gateway assignments against the site instrumentation register.
No validated common-cause reliability model is provided.
cards.applies_when: Several instruments show simultaneous changes, particularly paired taps or instruments sharing infrastructure.
cards.review_basis: Dependency-analysis guidance; confirm the site instrumentation dependencies before applying.
counterexamples: Eight taps on one shared conversion path are not eight independent witnesses.
An operating transient can also produce a coherent pressure pattern; attenuation alone cannot identify a leak.
Independent gateways do not exclude an unrecorded shared power or operating cause.
verification_steps: Compare near, farther and weak/quiet connected observers jointly, not only above-threshold supporters.
Contrast a shared-path instrument with an independent observer; compare profiles, valid-sample overlap and graph distances.
Inspect contradictory or asynchronous changes rather than merging branch-level earliest/latest timings into a common onset.
Open applicable maintenance records and check effective revision and scope.

cards.title: Test operating transients as competing explanations

sources.boundary: Review of pressure methods, operating transients and model assumptions; not a site-specific operating procedure.

cards.guidance: Investigate operating changes rather than equating a pressure anomaly with a leak. Compare the observed sign, timing and affected assets with an approved, incident-time-available record. A proposal is not an executed operation, and a superseded record is not current authority. Read the underlying records referenced by a coverage statement. A plausible explanation for one branch does not automatically explain a different pattern elsewhere. Incomplete logs cannot prove that no operation or leak occurred.
limitations: Temporal association is not a causal intervention.
The cited review includes liquid-pipeline methods; its parameters cannot be transferred directly to subsea gas.
cards.applies_when: Pressure changes could coincide with a valve, compressor, setpoint or calibration activity.
cards.review_basis: Research-grounded guidance; apply the current site operating procedure.
counterexamples: A broad positive operating shift does not by itself explain a separate localized negative region.
A real operating change can coexist with a leak or instrumentation fault.
verification_steps: Search affected and contrasting signal regions, not only the proposed inspection branch.
Open current records and distinguish planned, approved and executed activities.
Compare before/after periods near an observed change; note window censoring and retain missingness.

cards.title: Separate a numerical inspection bracket from physical leak localization

sources.boundary: Explains method-dependent localization assumptions; requires verification of site-specific inspection assumptions.

cards.guidance: Use the numerical tool's actual method and retain its assumptions. The default method brackets affected stations against unaffected neighbours. On extended networks, a broad continuous pressure footprint may leave no unaffected neighbours or an overly wide bracket. The pressure-peak-focus fallback can then identify a priority inspection focus from the final five seconds of fully observed paired readings: a unique contiguous pressure-deficit peak, agreeing pairs, independent comparison paths and weaker immediately neighbouring stations whose contrast exceeds the baseline-noise allowance. Missing comparisons, tied/disconnected peaks, inadequate independence and excessive width still withhold a focus. Those comparison stations need not be unaffected. This is a spatial pressure-focus heuristic, not a calibrated hydraulic inverse problem or a guarantee that a physical leak lies inside the interval. Pressure-wave localization requires justified propagation, timing, flow and pipeline assumptions. Do not infer an exact leak coordinate, leak size or leak probability from anomaly magnitude or a research formula without its inputs. Physical intervention still requires the approved site procedure and operator authorization.
limitations: The source review discusses methods with different fluid and deployment assumptions.
Confirm inspection priorities using independent pressure and flow measurements.
cards.applies_when: An engineer requests a leak location or an inspection recommendation from pressure observations.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived inspection guidance; confirm eligibility and site-specific hydraulic assumptions.
counterexamples: A larger pressure residual is not necessarily the nearest sensor to a leak.
Multiple disjoint pressure regions are not resolved by this single-leak bracket.
verification_steps: Check eligibility, paired coverage, observer independence, actual method and bounding comparisons.
State the priority interval and explain whether its neighbours are unaffected or simply weaker; do not call it a confidence interval or confirmed leak point.
Keep physical confirmation and operator authorization separate from the completed pressure-pattern assessment; do not clear alarms while waiting for an LLM.

cards.title: Expert-guided differential investigation program

sources.boundary: Architecture, expertise capture and open uncertainty/contradiction challenges; no subsea benchmark.

cards.guidance: Use this natural-language program to guide the existing read-only specialist workflow, not to assert an answer. Preserve competing leak, instrumentation and operating explanations. Select measurements and contextual checks that could distinguish them, including counterevidence. Apply only relevant knowledge, explicitly connect it to observed case evidence, and retain contradictions and missing prerequisites. Domain guidance supplies reasoning, not incident facts or authority to clear the numerical warning.
limitations: Inspired by DANA CAPTURE/APPLY and natural-language programs, not an OpenSSA or DanaOS implementation.
The paper's FinanceBench results do not establish pipeline diagnostic accuracy.
cards.applies_when: An anomaly episode requires a bounded, reviewable leak-versus-instrumentation RCA investigation.
cards.review_basis: DANA-inspired investigation program; apply site-reviewed expertise and operator approval.
counterexamples: Retrieving a relevant document without applying it is not RCA.
A well-cited but consistently wrong explanation is not successful expert reasoning.
verification_steps: Quality: establish what was measured reliably and what remains missing.
Diagnosis: inspect connectivity, independent domains and competing signal regions.
Diagnosis: choose relevant operational records and discriminating comparisons.
Response: explain which guidance was applied, supporting and contradicting case evidence, and remaining gaps.
Critic: check case facts and knowledge citations against their original pinned sources.
Handoff: request qualified engineer verification; unresolved evidence remains unresolved.

cards.guidance: An unusual reading is not itself a faulty sensor or a physical leak. Separate completeness, currentness, accuracy and provenance. Missing values and invalid sentinels are observation gaps, not measured pressure drops. Inspect persistence and paired disagreement, and seek an independent reference before attributing a hardware fault. A detector's attribution score identifies a contribution, not a physical root cause. Malfunction and a physical event can coexist.
limitations: This is a research-derived heuristic, not a field-approved sensor diagnosis.
No universal threshold or sensor-failure probability is established.
cards.applies_when: Pressure alerts coexist with missing samples, spikes, drift or inconsistent instrument readings.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived guidance; application requires site instrumentation review.
counterexamples: A gap during a real leak does not establish a healthy pipeline.
A genuine process transient can produce a large anomaly score on functioning instruments.
verification_steps: Compare suspect instruments with independent observers and their actual received coverage.
Check calibration, units, clock and maintenance context; preserve unobserved periods.
State which sensor claims were reviewed and which remain unchecked.

sources.reference: User-provided public defense deck, not redistributed

sources.boundary: Motivates prior knowledge and source-quality review; gateway independence requires site instrumentation verification.

cards.guidance: Inspect groups, not isolated alert flags. For pressure-monitoring investigations, a leak hypothesis should be tested against a sustained connected pattern: disruptive changes near the affected region and weaker, related changes farther along the pipes, including below-threshold observations. Compare synchronized profiles, relative magnitudes, timing, recovery and missingness against independent and contrasting instruments. Attenuation is not necessarily monotonic in real branched gas networks; this is a working hypothesis, not a universal law. Scattered impulses, isolated drift or missing data motivate instrumentation checks but can coexist with a leak. Treat hydraulic connectivity and instrumentation dependency as different relationships. Multiple agreeing instruments sharing a gateway, power supply or calibration path may share an error. Correlation is not independence or a confirmed cause. Shared-failure explanations also need observed evidence; do not declare every sensor on a gateway faulty from metadata alone.
limitations: Confirm A/B gateway assignments against the site instrumentation register.
No validated common-cause reliability model is provided.
cards.applies_when: Several instruments show simultaneous changes, particularly paired taps or instruments sharing infrastructure.
cards.review_basis: Dependency-analysis guidance; confirm the site instrumentation dependencies before applying.
counterexamples: Eight taps on one shared conversion path are not eight independent witnesses.
An operating transient can also produce a coherent pressure pattern; attenuation alone cannot identify a leak.
Independent gateways do not exclude an unrecorded shared power or operating cause.
verification_steps: Compare near, farther and weak/quiet connected observers jointly, not only above-threshold supporters.
Contrast a shared-path instrument with an independent observer; compare profiles, valid-sample overlap and graph distances.
Inspect contradictory or asynchronous changes rather than merging branch-level earliest/latest timings into a common onset.
Open applicable maintenance records and check effective revision and scope.

cards.title: Test operating transients as competing explanations

sources.boundary: Review of pressure methods, operating transients and model assumptions; not a site-specific operating procedure.

cards.guidance: Investigate operating changes rather than equating a pressure anomaly with a leak. Compare the observed sign, timing and affected assets with an approved, incident-time-available record. A proposal is not an executed operation, and a superseded record is not current authority. Read the underlying records referenced by a coverage statement. A plausible explanation for one branch does not automatically explain a different pattern elsewhere. Incomplete logs cannot prove that no operation or leak occurred.
limitations: Temporal association is not a causal intervention.

cards.title: Separate a numerical inspection bracket from physical leak localization

sources.boundary: Explains method-dependent localization assumptions; requires verification of site-specific inspection assumptions.

cards.guidance: Use the numerical tool's actual method and retain its assumptions. The default method brackets affected stations against unaffected neighbours. On extended networks, a broad continuous pressure footprint may leave no unaffected neighbours or an overly wide bracket. The pressure-peak-focus fallback can then identify a priority inspection focus from the final five seconds of fully observed paired readings: a unique contiguous pressure-deficit peak, agreeing pairs, independent comparison paths and weaker immediately neighbouring stations whose contrast exceeds the baseline-noise allowance. Missing comparisons, tied/disconnected peaks, inadequate independence and excessive width still withhold a focus. Those comparison stations need not be unaffected. This is a spatial pressure-focus heuristic, not a calibrated hydraulic inverse problem or a guarantee that a physical leak lies inside the interval. Pressure-wave localization requires justified propagation, timing, flow and pipeline assumptions. Do not infer an exact leak coordinate, leak size or leak probability from anomaly magnitude or a research formula without its inputs. Physical intervention still requires the approved site procedure and operator authorization.
limitations: The source review discusses methods with different fluid and deployment assumptions.
Confirm inspection priorities using independent pressure and flow measurements.
cards.applies_when: An engineer requests a leak location or an inspection recommendation from pressure observations.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived inspection guidance; confirm eligibility and site-specific hydraulic assumptions.
counterexamples: A larger pressure residual is not necessarily the nearest sensor to a leak.
Multiple disjoint pressure regions are not resolved by this single-leak bracket.
verification_steps: Check eligibility, paired coverage, observer independence, actual method and bounding comparisons.
State the priority interval and explain whether its neighbours are unaffected or simply weaker; do not call it a confidence interval or confirmed leak point.
Keep physical confirmation and operator authorization separate from the completed pressure-pattern assessment; do not clear alarms while waiting for an LLM.

cards.title: Distinguish unreliable observations from physical process evidence

sources.boundary: Marine data-quality and anomaly-attribution principles; not validation of gas-pipeline leak classification.

cards.guidance: An unusual reading is not itself a faulty sensor or a physical leak. Separate completeness, currentness, accuracy and provenance. Missing values and invalid sentinels are observation gaps, not measured pressure drops. Inspect persistence and paired disagreement, and seek an independent reference before attributing a hardware fault. A detector's attribution score identifies a contribution, not a physical root cause. Malfunction and a physical event can coexist.
limitations: This is a research-derived heuristic, not a field-approved sensor diagnosis.
No universal threshold or sensor-failure probability is established.

sources.boundary: Strong, possible, lower-threshold and noisy detections motivate multiscale inspection; not calibrated gas-pipeline attenuation.

sources.boundary: Motivates prior knowledge and source-quality review; gateway independence requires site instrumentation verification.

cards.guidance: Inspect groups, not isolated alert flags. For pressure-monitoring investigations, a leak hypothesis should be tested against a sustained connected pattern: disruptive changes near the affected region and weaker, related changes farther along the pipes, including below-threshold observations. Compare synchronized profiles, relative magnitudes, timing, recovery and missingness against independent and contrasting instruments. Attenuation is not necessarily monotonic in real branched gas networks; this is a working hypothesis, not a universal law. Scattered impulses, isolated drift or missing data motivate instrumentation checks but can coexist with a leak. Treat hydraulic connectivity and instrumentation dependency as different relationships. Multiple agreeing instruments sharing a gateway, power supply or calibration path may share an error. Correlation is not independence or a confirmed cause. Shared-failure explanations also need observed evidence; do not declare every sensor on a gateway faulty from metadata alone.
limitations: Confirm A/B gateway assignments against the site instrumentation register.
No validated common-cause reliability model is provided.

Decision
Prioritize P5 integrity review at 600-1000 m along the pipe, around stations ST4/ST5 at 700/900 m: its joint pressure deficit supports a suspected integrity incident. This accepted inspection interval is a pressure-focus heuristic, not a confirmed leak point or dispatch approval [ev-227; KN-LOCALIZATION-R1]. Keep P7 on shared-connection checks, P2 on operating-transition/process review, P4 on secondary pressure/process review plus a separate instrument check, and P1/P3/P6 on instrument checks.

Your first actions
1. Scope the read-only P5 integrity review to the accepted interval, distinguishing this suspected-source inspection priority from the wider pressure-event footprint [ev-227; KN-LOCALIZATION-R1].
2. Keep gateway-P7-0, the shared data connection for P7's odd-numbered stations, on the instrumentation track rather than counting eight taps as independent leak witnesses [MAINT-P7-GW-002; KN-INDEPENDENCE-R1].
3. Use the reviewed P2 record to distinguish its 90-145-second transition from later deficits; retain P4's weaker losses as unresolved secondary pressure changes [OP-P2-EXTENDED-001; subsea_36beb72cf0a14e67b4405625f86ee2a1].
4. Seek independent physical pressure and flow confirmation at the P5 focus and a pressure reference outside P7's shared connection to distinguish physical loss from a reading offset.

Already checked
Profiles show gradual upward drift at P1-ST6-A, downward drift at P3-ST7-A, brief spikes at P4-ST7-B and P6-ST3-A, and a later flatline, or stuck reading, at P6-ST8-B; their paired comparison sensors remain distinct [185711a2-c736-53e6-8880-7ca84786d661; 0310aa00-fcb4-59e7-aef2-bc6fa4b1c846]. P7-ST1-A/B, ST3-A/B, ST5-A/B and ST7-A/B show a shared persistent offset, not confirmed individual hardware failures. Coverage is 99.18%, but health review is partial: P1-ST7-B and P3-ST5-B each lack 20 of 60 expected readings; P4-ST8-A has 15 invalid received readings out of 60 [ev-225; ev-027; ev-083; ev-125; KN-QUALITY-R1].

Why this decision
In the final five seconds, elapsed 355-360 seconds in the recording, P5-ST4-A is 1.680 bar below the supplied normal reference, versus 1.243 bar at neighbouring P5-ST3-A; bar is a pressure unit [ev-142; ev-138]. Agreeing pairs across both P5 connections and sustained profiles support its priority. P2-ST8-A and P4-ST1-A show smaller deficits of 0.189 and 0.209 bar [ev-062; ev-098]. Their relationship to P5 remains unresolved: weaker connected-branch changes can accompany one incident, but hydraulic propagation is not established. P2 screening flags do not establish unreliable readings.

What changes the decision
An independently confirmed sustained P7 loss outside its shared connection, deterioration of P5's focus, or a supported P5 operating explanation would change the ranking. The opened log is incomplete and supplies no verified P5 action; pressure patterns cannot confirm the physical cause [LOG-EXTENDED-COVERAGE-001].
